scope: Active voucher creation sites detected by scripts/audit-write-evidence.mjs after excluding updates/deletes/restores/moves of existing voucher rows. Completed phases are retained separately as historical evidence and must not re-enter the active backlog.

explicit-replay-guard.verdict: documented compatibility exemption with an explicit replay/source guard
explicit-replay-guard.reason: These pre-existing creation sites are protected by an existing-voucher/source-row check, atomic state claim, conflict handling, or replace-in-transaction semantics. Phase 7 freezes this exact reviewed set: no new raw voucher creator may join it without an explicit review-file exemption, so direct voucher creation can no longer grow silently.

phase-3-infrastructure-writers.verdict: phase 3 completed with required deterministic posting identity
phase-3-infrastructure-writers.reason: These lower-level voucher writers use the durable accounting posting request identity boundary. They require stable business/request source identity, serialize identical concurrent retries, reuse matching vouchers, reject changed payloads under a reused key, and clean identity markers before intentional hard-delete/rebuild operations.

phase-4-operational-writers.verdict: phase 4 completed behind the durable operational request boundary
phase-4-operational-writers.reason: These highest-risk manual voucher, payroll, advance, employee cash/POS and supplier-payment writers are registered behind one company-scoped request boundary. Browser and offline retries reuse a persisted clientRequestId; the server atomically reserves (company, idempotency key), fingerprints method/path/payload, blocks duplicate execution, waits for an identical in-flight request, replays the stored response after completion, rejects changed payloads under the same key, and fails closed when the first outcome is uncertain.

phase-5-operational-writers.verdict: phase 5 completed behind the durable operational request boundary
phase-5-operational-writers.reason: The final operational families now receive browser/offline-stable client request identity and are claimed by a company-scoped durable server boundary before the legacy handlers execute. Identical retries/concurrent submissions replay one result; changed payload under a reused identity conflicts; uncertain outcomes fail closed.

phase-6-deterministic-source-writers.verdict: phase 6 completed with deterministic durable source identity
phase-6-deterministic-source-writers.reason: These special-purpose routes are not given browser-generated request IDs. The server derives a stable migration/import/repair source key from the operation kind, target company and canonical source payload (or an explicit sourceRunId/importBatchId), persists that key before execution, replays completed reruns, rejects changed data under a reused key, releases definite validation failures, and fails closed on uncertain server outcomes.

phase-6-intrinsic-replay-safe-writers.verdict: phase 6 completed by durable business-state replay proof
phase-6-intrinsic-replay-safe-writers.reason: These writers already derive safety from persistent business state rather than a browser request: payroll migration rewrites only old-account vouchers, company import requires an empty target, payroll backfill excludes payroll IDs that already have vouchers, rental re-accrue only corrects still-detectable discrepancies, and deferred-rent reclassification uses a per-company advisory lock and journals only the current remaining balance.

phase-7-post-review-safe-writers.verdict: post-review creator already protected by durable stock-document request identity
phase-7-post-review-safe-writers.reason: This stock-transfer creator entered the live tree after the original 81-file voucher review. Its create-from-scratch branch already consumes clientRequestId, uses the stock-document idempotency key/marker inside the transfer transaction, replays the existing transfer on retry, and is protected by the global accounting request identity client path. Phase 7 records it explicitly so the direct-creation audit can distinguish reviewed growth from an unprotected escape hatch.

phase-8-request-identity-writers.verdict: reviewed compatibility creator whose write path now carries a durable request identity
phase-8-request-identity-writers.reason: server/routes/offloadRoutes.ts was reviewed as an explicit replay-guard creator because its post-offload charge backfill checked for the voucher it was about to write. Its other voucher-affecting path, the offload optional toggle, moved into services/containers/offloadOptionalToggle.ts behind withDurableFinancialOperation, a transaction-owned state guard and container/offload row locks, so the file now carries a stable request identity and is credited out of the measured backlog. The backfill creator that remains in this file keeps the documented existing-voucher replay check, and the file stays in this inventory so the direct-creation audit still accounts for it.

phase7DirectCreationPolicy.rule: Any server file that directly inserts a vouchers row must already appear in this reviewed/completed inventory. A new direct creator fails audit-write-evidence until it is moved through an approved canonical writer or explicitly documented as a restoration/recovery compatibility exemption.
